target.title: fix(nodes): resolve Unicode browser node names when configured by display name
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Browser gateway requests could fail to select a browser-capable node by display name when the node name used non-ASCII letters or numbers. The Browser gateway had its own ASCII-only matcher, while the shared node matcher is the canonical path used by sibling node-selection flows.

## Why This Change Was Made
The shared node-name normalizer now preserves Unicode letters and numbers while still treating punctuation-only queries as unknown. The Browser gateway now delegates node selection to the shared resolver instead of carrying a local duplicate matcher, so node id, remote IP, display name, and prefix matching stay consistent in one owner-local path.

## User Impact
Users can target browser nodes by Unicode display names without needing to copy a node id or IP address. Ambiguous and unknown node behavior remains handled by the shared resolver.

## Evidence
- Claim proved at `dda1b705f18f7737f17da1ae13a29548d3fedbd5`: Unicode node display names are preserved by shared matching, punctuation-only queries stay unknown, and the Browser gateway uses the shared resolver.
- Focused test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/node-match.test.ts` passed in the Docker lane with 9 tests passing.
- Focused test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/gateway/browser-request.profile-from-body.test.ts` passed in the Docker lane with 10 tests passing.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python3 .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
